messages:
Bob (Acme Mobile): Hey team — after we rotated our API key this morning, our Android app started getting 401s. Error payload: {"error":"invalid_api_key"}. We copied the new key from the dashboard and pushed it via our release pipeline.

Alice (Support): Sorry about that, Bob. Can you paste the request-id from one of the 401 responses and the exact Authorization header you send (obscure the key)? Also are you using the Redwood mobile SDK or raw HTTP calls?

Bob (Acme Mobile): Request-id: req_8f3b9d2a. Header we send (redacted): Authorization: Bearer sk_live_XXXXXXXXNEW. We're using Android app with our own HTTP client (okhttp) and we write the key into Android Keystore at build time. Example curl we tried from the app server:

```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_XXXXXXXXNEW" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  https://api.redwood.inference/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
```

Alice (Support): Thanks. Two quick checks: 1) can you run the same curl from your laptop (outside CI/mobile) to confirm whether the key is valid from a different environment; 2) confirm the key id prefix (sk_live_ vs rk_ etc) and whether the key was created under Hosted vs Dedicated for your org.

Bob (Acme Mobile): I ran curl from my laptop with the same header and I also get 401. Here is a full response we captured from the laptop test:

```
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
Content-Type: application/json
X-Request-ID: req_8f3f0000
Date: Tue, 18 Jan 2024 10:12:34 GMT

{"error":"invalid_api_key","message":"The API key provided is invalid."}
```

Alice (Support): Ok that's helpful — this means the key itself is being rejected by the auth service, not just a mobile interceptor. @infra-bot can you pull audit entries for key rotations for Acme org around 1713567000-1713567300? Also please check any auth-cache invalidation jobs.

infra-bot: Audit: key rotation for org=acme by jsmith at 1713567200 — old_key=sk_live_OLD -> new_key=sk_live_XXXXXXXXNEW. Key type=hosted, scopes=[generate,embeddings]. Cache invalidation job queued at 1713567230.

Sam (SRE): Two quick hypotheses: 1) The key in the dashboard wasn't fully activated (rare), or 2) CI/release pipeline modified the key value at build time (string templating issue). Also long-lived backend connections / keepalive shouldn't cause server-side invalidation issues, since curl from laptop also failed.

Alice (Support): Can you also confirm there are no accidental suffixes/prefixes added by CI variables? E.g. '${API_KEY}-${BUILD_NUMBER}' or similar. Sometimes build templating concatenates metadata.

Bob (Acme Mobile): I dug into our Gradle release task. We found a bad template in our CI environment file that concatenates the build tag to the api key variable:```
API_KEY="${API_KEY}-${BUILD_NUMBER}"
```
When we inject into Android Keystore the literal string includes the "-BUILD123" suffix for release builds. Dev builds used the raw key and worked earlier. We tested: copying the key shown in the dashboard and appending "-BUILD123" locally reproduces the 401.

Alice (Support): Nice find — that would definitely make the key invalid. Two remediation steps: 1) Remove the suffix in the CI template and rebuild, or 2) rotate to a fresh key and update pipeline to use exact value (recommended: rotate and cut a new key). We'll also check auth logs to ensure no partial activation issues.

Sam (SRE): Confirmed in auth logs: requests with Authorization header containing suffix "-BUILD123" map to failed lookup — no matching key id. Keys without suffix accepted. No issue on Redwood side other than invalid credential value.

Bob (Acme Mobile): Thanks — we'll patch CI, rebuild and push a hotfix. For now we've rotated to a new key and verified curl from laptop succeeds once the suffix is removed.

Alice (Support): Great. Marking as resolved from Support side. Recommendations captured: rotate key, fix CI variable templating, add a sanity check in release pipeline (curl -I call with the key post-build), and consider short test-run using the new key before pushing to production. Thanks @Sam and @infra-bot for the logs. :thumbsup:

Bob (Acme Mobile): Appreciated — saved us a ton of time. Closing the thread.
